Morristown.metaDescription: Raccoons, bats, squirrels, and skunks in Morristown, VT — Morrisville village homes, Lamoille River farms, and homes toward Stowe. Same-day service — call us today.
Morristown.housing_era: The town of Morristown centers on the village of Morrisville, with older village homes and a small downtown, farmhouses along the Lamoille River, and rural and newer homes on the roads toward Hyde Park, Stowe, and Elmore.
Morristown.geographic_features: Lamoille River (flows through Morrisville in a wide valley), Lake Lamoille (small lake on the river west of the village), Cadys Falls (river falls in the western part of town), Elmore Mountain foothills (wooded ridges along the southern border)

Morristown.wildlife_intro:
Morristown's calls run from Morrisville's older village homes — attic bats, chimney raccoons, and squirrels in the street trees — out to Lamoille valley farms with barn raccoons, skunks, and woodchucks. Lake Lamoille and the river corridors keep beavers active on the brooks, and the wooded roads toward Elmore and Stowe add porcupines and red squirrels at camps and rural homes through the winter.

Fall is busy here, with rodents and squirrels entering homes before snow and hunters' camps needing closing. Spring brings denning raccoons and skunks, and summer bat colonies are exclusion only — one-way doors in spring and late August through fall, proofing from December through March, and no colony work while pups cannot fly. Our crew is in Morrisville and the valley towns weekly, so call us and we will fit you in.

faqs.q: Are beavers a problem around Morristown?
faqs.a: Along the Lamoille's side brooks and near Lake Lamoille, yes — dams can flood driveways, fields, and septic areas, especially in spring and fall. Our crew can evaluate a pond-leveling pipe for sites that can tolerate some water, or arrange licensed trapping where flooding threatens property. Relocating furbearers is prohibited in Vermont.

Stowe.wildlife_intro:
Stowe's wildlife problem is the quiet house. Village homes get the standard mix — squirrels, bats, chimney raccoons — but the Mountain Road condos and second homes across town sit empty for weeks, and mice, squirrels, bats, and the occasional porcupine move in unnoticed. The Mansfield forest edge is never far, so animals are always close, and a single unsealed gap can host a whole season of damage before anyone visits.

Our crew does opening and closing checks for many Stowe homes: proof in fall, inspect in spring, and deal with whatever winter left behind. Bat colonies in second homes are handled by exclusion only, timed for spring or late August through November — winter is for proofing an empty house, and no colony work happens while pups cannot fly. If your Stowe place sits empty between seasons, call us and we will keep it sealed.

faqs.q: How do I keep mice out of a Stowe condo that sits empty all mud season?

A sealed condo needs no poison and gives you a clean arrival instead of a cleanup.

Red squirrels and porcupines trouble the wooded homes on the valley sides.

Student rentals and farmhouses share the same fall rush — everything wants in before a Lamoille County winter. faqs.q: Why do Johnson rental homes get repeat wildlife calls?
